findings.summary: AGENTS.md — the Codex agent-instructions file this repo READS (gate-manifest.json, hooks/scripts/intent_nudge.py) — was hand-maintained and had rotted to carrying the PRE-v1.32.0 calibration section: 'calibration is not optional', the 14-day clock, the staleness release gate. All reversed days earlier. A Codex session following it would have done the opposite of current doctrine and no gate said so. Now generated from CLAUDE.md verbatim plus a curated host header, pinned byte-exact, with a hand-edit plant.

The rotted mirror came from a Claude->Codex find-replace leaving 12 artifacts, including a capitalised .Codex path (Codex uses lowercase) and a rewritten binary name where calibration needs the CLAUDE cli on every host. A prose substitution cannot distinguish a host name from a product name and fails silently, so the generator transforms NOTHING. Both failure shapes are frozen as plants.

tag_guard BLOCKED this release commit because the commit MESSAGE quoted the tag command as instructions for David, and a shell-statement scanner cannot tell a heredoc body from an executed statement without real shell parsing. It then blocked the guard_note record too, because filing the incident required quoting the same text — the report contains its own trigger. Disposition: the guard was RIGHT to be conservative here (a heredoc exemption would be trivially abusable), the block was accepted, the message was reworded, and no tag was created by any route. Recorded via guard_note so it appears as an ACCOUNTED block rather than an unaccounted one, and named here as a known ALLOW-direction limitation.
